memories.text: Restarting checkout-api for database connection pool exhaustion resolved nothing. The service recovered for roughly 20 minutes and the incident recurred three times in 24 hours. The cause was a deploy that lowered db_pool_max, which a restart cannot undo.
Operator correction on checkout-api incidents: check the deploy history before restarting anything. A restart hides a bad release and makes the next occurrence harder to diagnose.

Raising db_pool_max on checkout-api from 10 to 60 resolved database connection pool exhaustion. The change was applied as a config rollout, not a code deploy, and the error rate returned to baseline within four minutes.
The on-call operator wants a status-page update posted within 10 minutes of any incident rated major or above, and never wants to be paged below major severity.

checkout-api is owned by the Payments Platform team, whose on-call rotation is payments-primary. Its database pool is configured by db_pool_max, which ships at a default of 10 and is not sized for peak concurrency.
checkout-api carries a 99.9% monthly availability SLO and a p95 latency target of 800ms. Paging is warranted once the burn rate exceeds 2x over a 30-minute window.

Correlating a symptom's onset with the nearest deploy boundary has been the fastest route to root cause on this estate: in recent months it identified the cause on the first attempt more often than log search alone.
Scaling search-api from 4 to 8 replicas relieved a queue backlog during a traffic spike. Whether this generalises to other services is unconfirmed.

A rollback of payments-api was attempted for an unrelated latency regression and did not help; the cause turned out to be an upstream dependency. Recorded so a future run does not assume a rollback is always the answer.
Post-incident write-ups on this team are expected to name the specific config key or commit that caused the incident, not just the service.
On checkout-api, rolling back the deploy that lowered db_pool_max resolved connection pool exhaustion; the error rate returned below 1% and was confirmed by a health check.
